title: Follow-ups: the experience harness, the TV browser gate and the tool audit able to fail when they should, and the README and deploy guide saying what production is
requested_outcome:
Fourteen follow-ups from the round-12 deploy review, filed as work for the next build under the owner's ship rule of 30 September. None changes what CLIVE does for the owner: each makes a check able to fail when it should, or a document say what is true. Fix each with a test that fails on the code at the base commit (the documents excepted).
- X1/X1-01 (experience/harness.py _fits, model_could_make): it claims to check that Claude could make a scripted call, but checks only the top-level type and enum; a missing nested required field, a wrong array item or a number outside its bounds passes.
- X1/X1-02 (experience/scenarios.py LIVE_SCENARIOS, needs_reply): the scenario runs live but requires rows before its live/fixture split, so a healthy real inbox with nobody waiting fails it.
- R9-H-experience1-H-05 (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; experience/scenarios.py needs_reply): the oracle compares sets of thread ids, so duplicated queue rows pass as the expected threads.
- X1/X1-04 (experience/matrix.py COVERAGE['model_turn'], build): the whole model_turn row is marked live-read-safe because it has scenarios, though some stage discount, order-edit and email writes and the live allow-list is narrower.
- X2/X2-02 (experience/scenario_packs/abandoned.py abandoned_window): any count at or below the fortnight's passes, zero included, and any read mentioning 'abandoned' is taken as proof the seven-day filter reached Shopify.
- X2/X2-01 (experience/tv_flow.py run): the driver's last JSON is forwarded without checking node's exit status or that every mode and change was measured.
- SC1/SC1-01 (scripts/browser/tv_flow.js main, walkMode): report.ok stays true when page errors were recorded or a new view never became readable (ready_ms null); only an exception fails it.
- R9-I-tests5-I-05 (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; experience/tool_matrix.py read_test): the audit counts a dispatch inside a helper that no test calls; tests/test_tool_matrix.py's positive case accepts an uncalled go().
- R9-H-experience1-H-06 (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; experience/tool_matrix.py scenario_strings, _scenario_tools): string literals are still collected outside a few excluded forms, and a collected tool name counts as coverage.
- R9-H-experience1-F-A2-FIXTURE (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; experience/harness.py harness): the harness puts back app.state.runtime and allowed_logins, but its lifespan leaves app.state.housekeeper holding the fixture runtime.
- DOC2/DOC2-02 (experience/tool_matrix.py, the text it writes): the matrix classes screen_show, screen_off and the other screen tools as reads and says reads never mutate, though they change what a screen shows.
- DOC1/DOC1-01 (README.md, 'Who may ask'): it says requests made on the host itself are always allowed; on the Linux production host, with local-owner access off, a request made on the host is not an owner request.
- DOC1/DOC1-02 (README.md, 'Changes to the store and the inbox'): the list and its count ('nine changes') leave out making a new order by voice and the other changes CLIVE can now prepare.
- DOC2/DOC2-01 (docs/DEPLOY_LINUX.md, 'Running as root — temporary'): it lists writes being off as a safeguard; production runs with writes on, behind the owner's hold.
Every document change is written from the code and configuration at the base commit (config/settings.py, app/main.py, the write tools), not from memory.

What must not change, in every part of this build: every sentence the owner types or says still goes to the model exactly as said, and nothing here reads, answers or routes a sentence by a word list in front of it (deterministic code may check what the model did, never decide for it); every change to the shop or to email stays behind the owner's hold-to-confirm card, nothing here adds a write or skips staging, confirmation or verification, and reads stay reads; no private business data goes into git, and every name, address and order in a test is invented; no test assertion is weakened (an assertion changed here is made stricter, and the report names each one); the kernel, the gate, secret scanning and the acceptance machinery are untouched, and no protected path is edited (protected tests such as tests/test_compose.py, tests/test_engineering_bridge.py and tests/conftest.py are run, never changed); docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md is regenerated by the loop and never edited by hand. Plain British English in comments and docstrings that say what is true and why; no placeholder copy, invented defaults or filler.
acceptance_criteria: X1-01: model_could_make refuses, with a reason, a call missing a nested object's required field, an array item of the wrong type, a number outside its minimum or maximum, and a string past its maxLength; every golden scenario's scripted calls still pass it (tests/test_experience.py).
X1-02: run live, needs_reply passes an empty queue when its count is 0 and the answer says nobody is waiting; the fixture run still requires the exact, non-empty waiting threads.
R9-H-experience1-H-05: a queue that repeats a waiting thread fails the needs_reply oracle (rows compared as a list or a count of each, not a set).
X1-04: the model_turn row is live-read-safe only if every scenario under it is in LIVE_SCENARIOS and stages no write; otherwise the matrix says it is not, and a test pins it.

X2-02: abandoned_window compares the answer's seven-day count and value with _window(7) exactly and asserts that the recorded Shopify request carries the seven-day date filter; zero where the fixture has checkouts in the window fails.

X2-01: tv_flow.run returns ok false, with the reason, when the driver exits non-zero, or when any mode or any expected change is missing from its results; tested with a stand-in driver, with no browser.

SC1-01: tv_flow.js's verdict is false when any page error was recorded, when any step has no readable result, or when a measured time is over the limit it claims; the verdict is a function that tests/web/followups-tv-flow.test.js exercises.

R9-I-tests5-I-05: the audit credits a dispatch inside a helper only when a test function in the same file calls that helper, directly or through other helpers; a dispatch in an uncalled async def go() credits nothing, and tests/test_tool_matrix.py's case is changed to say so (named in the report as a legitimately moved, stricter case).

R9-H-experience1-H-06: a tool name that a scenario holds only as data it never hands on (an unused constant, a label or message string, a dict or list never passed to the scripted model, dispatch or a staging command) credits no coverage; tested with such a scenario source.

R9-H-experience1-F-A2-FIXTURE: after harness() exits, every attribute its lifespan set on app.state (housekeeper included) is as it was before, and every binding runtime.build() made is put back; a test enters and leaves the harness and checks.

DOC2-02: the matrix text written by experience/tool_matrix.py says that 'read' there means the write-spec and read-scheduler boundary, not that nothing changes, and names the screen tools that change what a screen shows; TOOL_MATRIX.md is left to the loop's regeneration.

DOC1-01: README's 'Who may ask' tells the Mac's rule apart from the Linux production host's, and says that on production, with local-owner access off, a request made on the host is not an owner request; owner requests come through Tailscale from a login on the allow-list.

DOC1-02: README's list of changes and its count match the writes CLIVE can prepare at the base commit, including a new order made by voice (a Shopify draft, completed only on his hold), each with its gesture and how it is proven.
DOC2-01: DEPLOY_LINUX's 'Running as root' no longer lists writes being off as a safeguard; it says production runs with writes on behind the owner's hold, and names the switches that stay off.

The new tests are in tests/test_followups_harness.py, which also runs tests/web/followups-tv-flow.test.js under node (skipped only where node is absent, with '# fail 0' asserted); each fails on the base code; tests/test_experience.py, tests/test_tool_matrix.py, tests/test_r11_families.py (the README test) and tests/test_r13_evidence_index.py still pass.
